Wrath

/RATH/ - rhymes with math · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Wrath means fierce, vengeful anger.

In the comic strip, the baker's wrath is the town's weather: shortchange her once and your bread order is doomed for a season.

Worked Example

The exiled vizier fled not the sultan's law but his wrath — the law would have fined him; the wrath wanted his head.

Wrath is anger at its grandest and most vengeful. Rage flares and burns out; wrath remembers, plans, and repays. The word survives mostly where the stakes are epic — gods, kings, prophets — which is exactly the weight it lends a sentence.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fury: blazing, violent anger in the moment

rage: overwhelming anger that can slip control

ire: a literary word for anger, milder than wrath

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

serenity: untroubled calm no insult can reach

mildness: a temper too gentle to seek payback

Where it sits · how much payback the feeling demands — annoyance → anger → wrath

annoyance vs. wrath: Annoyance is a pebble in the shoe — nowhere near wrath's gathering storm.

anger vs. wrath: Plain anger runs hot and passes; it stops short of wrath, which is fierce and wants repayment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — wra

Root — wra: angry (Old English wrath, 'furious')

Suffix — -th

Suffix — -th: noun ending: state of (as in warmth, growth)

Put it together

Put it together: Wra (angry — Old English wrath) + -th (the state-of ending in warmth and growth) = the state of being furious. English built wrath at home, the same way it built warmth from warm; the old adjective survives only in the archaic wroth — 'the king waxed wroth.'

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Wrath's adjective, wroth, is archaic, and the deeper root — likely the same 'twist' that gave us writhe, anger as being twisted tight — is prehistoric guesswork. So there is no everyday relative to build from: wrath stands alone, with a noun's full weight.

Strength Check

Word Choice

literary / grand

Wrath is anger at epic scale with vengeance in it — gods, kings, storms. Everyday fury does fine for traffic. In this unit's anger family, rancor is slow and cold, a tirade is anger talking, and wrath is anger acting; when unsure, ask whether the anger wants payback.
